members.revoke_invitation_description: Revoke the invitation to {{email}}? They will no longer be able to join this workspace.
members.remove_member_description: Remove {{name}} from {{workspace}}? They lose access, and the keys and packages delivered by this workspace are revoked from their machines.
members.perimeter_description: Corporate MCP presets and perimeter tools
members.cannot_demote_last_owner_title: Promote another member to owner first — a workspace must keep at least one owner.
members.remove_member_unavailable: This member has neither a display name nor an email to type, so the removal cannot be confirmed here.
members.role_promote_admin_description: {{name}} will be able to set the gateway address and key for the whole workspace, put a key into any member's personal layer, edit the provisioning pins every machine obeys, remove any member who is not an owner - which disarms that member's machines - and grant perimeter access, including to themselves. They will also be able to manage the integration keys other members have already entered: environment variables in someone else's agent can be added, replaced and removed, and an MCP server can be removed, all without Goosar showing them a stored value. Adding or changing an MCP server on an agent they do not own stays with that agent's owner, because such a server is a command that runs on the owner's machine. What no role setting controls is the machine an agent runs on: whoever hosts that runtime receives the agent's values in plaintext.
members.role_promote_owner_description: On top of everything an admin can do, {{name}} will be able to delete {{workspace}} and to change or remove other owners, including you. If they remove you first, you cannot take this back.
members.role_demote_owner_to_admin_description: {{name}} keeps admin rights but loses the right to delete {{workspace}} and to manage other owners, so they can no longer undo your decisions or remove you. Their machines, agents and work are untouched.
members.role_demote_owner_to_member_description: {{name}} loses the right to delete {{workspace}} and to manage other owners, and with it access to the workspace configuration and keys, to the provisioning pins and to member management. Their machines, agents and work are untouched.
members.role_demote_admin_description: {{name}} loses access to the workspace configuration and its keys, to the provisioning pins, to member management and to editing other people's agents, skills and runtimes. Their own machines, agents and tasks are untouched, and perimeter access, if granted, stays granted.
members.role_change_unavailable: This member has neither a display name nor an email to type, so the role change cannot be confirmed here.
members.perimeter_grant_description: {{name}}'s Helper gets seeded with the corporate MCP preset catalog, and onboarding starts asking them for corporate tokens. Seeding happens once and is not undone by revoking access — to take it back you have to remove {{name}} from the workspace.
members.perimeter_revoke_description: This only stops future delivery: onboarding stops asking for corporate tokens and a new Helper is no longer seeded. Nothing already delivered is withdrawn — the seeded presets and the tokens {{name}} entered stay on their machines. To actually close access, remove {{name}} from the workspace and rotate the gateway key.
members.invite_admin_description: Once they accept, {{email}} will be able to set the gateway address and key for the whole workspace, put a key into any member's personal layer, edit the provisioning pins every machine obeys, remove any member who is not an owner and grant perimeter access. Until they accept, the invitation sits in the pending list and can be revoked.

pins.title: Provisioning pins
pins.description: Which packages of the deployment catalog this workspace provisions to members' machines.
pins.no_pins_banner: No pins: the machines receive the whole deployment catalog.
pins.all_disabled_banner: Every pin is disabled: the machines provision nothing.
pins.empty_catalog: Nothing is published in the deployment catalog yet.
pins.stale_enable_blocked: This package is no longer in the deployment catalog. Turning the pin on would break provisioning for the whole workspace, so it stays off until the package is published again.
pins.first_pin_dialog_description: This workspace has no pins, so its machines receive the whole deployment catalog. Pinning {{name}} narrows delivery to {{name}} and the packages it requires: every other package already delivered is removed from members' machines on their next sync.
pins.unpin_dialog_description: The pin is removed and {{name}} stops being delivered: the copies already on members' machines are removed on their next sync. The other enabled pins keep being delivered.
pins.unpin_inactive_dialog_description: This pin is already turned off, so {{name}} is not delivered and has already been removed from members' machines. Removing the pin changes nothing there, and the other pins are untouched.
pins.unpin_last_dialog_description: This is the only pin left, so removing it does not revoke {{name}}. With no pins the workspace provisions the whole deployment catalog again: every published package is delivered to every member's machines on their next sync.
pins.unpin_unavailable: This pin has no package name, so there is nothing to type and it cannot be revoked here. Removing all pins would not revoke it either — that only widens delivery back to the whole catalog.
pins.disable_dialog_description: The pin stays, but {{name}} is no longer delivered and the copies already on members' machines are removed on their next sync. The other enabled pins keep being delivered.
pins.disable_last_dialog_description: {{name}} is the last enabled pin. Turning it off leaves the workspace with no enabled pin at all, so its machines provision nothing: every package this workspace delivered is removed from every member's machine on their next sync.
pins.reset_dialog_description: Every pin is removed (now: {{total}}). This is not a revocation: with no pins the workspace provisions the whole deployment catalog again, so every published package is delivered to every member's machines on their next sync. Only a pinned package that is no longer in the catalog disappears from them.
pins.workspace_unavailable: This workspace has no name to type, so a change that reaches the whole workspace cannot be confirmed here.
pins.broken_banner: Delivery is down for this workspace: {{name}} is pinned and turned on, but the deployment catalog does not publish version {{version}} of it, so every member's machine gets an error instead of packages. Turning that pin off — or removing it — starts delivering the other pins again.
pins.broken_banner_dependency: Provisioning is stopped for this workspace right now: {{name}}@{{version}} is required by a pinned package but is no longer in the deployment catalog, so every machine gets an error instead of packages. It is not in the list below — publish it again, or turn off the pin that requires it.
pins.collateral_line: Along with it, packages that only {{name}} pulled in leave every machine as well: {{names}}.
pins.catalog_unknown_banner: The deployment catalog cannot be read right now. The pins below are shown as saved, but which of them the catalog still publishes is unknown, so nothing here is marked as missing.
pins.stale_version_enable_blocked: The deployment catalog no longer publishes version {{version}} of {{name}}. Turning the pin on would break delivery for the whole workspace, so it stays off until this version is published again.
pins.lockfile_pin: {{name}} is added to the pins and turned on.
pins.lockfile_disable: The pin for {{name}} stays but is turned off.
pins.effect_unknown: The deployment catalog cannot be read right now, so what members' machines start or stop receiving cannot be shown here.
pins.effect_repair: Delivery is down for this workspace right now: an enabled pin is not in the deployment catalog, so members' machines get an error instead of packages. This change lets the other enabled pins be delivered again.
pins.effect_still_broken: Delivery stays down after this: another enabled pin is not in the deployment catalog either, so members' machines keep getting an error until that pin is turned off too.
pins.effect_stale_dropped: {{name}} itself stops being delivered, so the copies still on members' machines are removed once delivery recovers.
pins.unpin_kept_dialog_description: The pin is removed, but {{name}} keeps being delivered: another enabled pin requires it. Nothing is removed from members' machines.
pins.disable_kept_dialog_description: The pin stays and is turned off, but {{name}} keeps being delivered: another enabled pin requires it. Nothing is removed from members' machines.
pins.unpin_stop_dialog_description: {{name}} is the last enabled pin. Removing it leaves only pins that are turned off, so the workspace delivers nothing at all: every package it delivered is removed from every member's machine on their next sync.
pins.first_pin_no_change_description: This workspace has no pins, so its machines receive the whole deployment catalog. Pinning {{name}} changes nothing for them: {{name}} and the packages it requires are everything the catalog publishes today.
pins.effect_breaks: After this change the deployment catalog can no longer be resolved for this workspace, so every member's machine gets an error instead of packages until the missing package is published or the pins are put back.
pins.effect_repair_unpinned: Delivery is down for this workspace right now: an enabled pin is not in the deployment catalog, so members' machines get an error instead of packages. With no pins left the workspace delivers the whole deployment catalog again.
pins.requires_enable_blocked: The deployment catalog does not publish everything {{name}} requires, so turning the pin on would break delivery for the whole workspace. It stays off until the missing package is published.

typed_confirm.target_unavailable: There is no exact value to type here, so this action cannot be confirmed.

deployment.description: Deployment-level administration: the deployment admin role and the policy layer every workspace inherits. The policy never carries credentials.

admins.title: Deployment administrators
admins.description: Composition changes are filed as pending requests and take effect only after an operator confirms them on the server.
admins.add_hint: By email of an existing user. The grant stays pending until confirmed on the server.
admins.email_aria: Email of the user to grant the role to
admins.remove_aria: Request revoking the deployment admin role from {{name}}
admins.confirm_instruction: To apply, confirm on the server:

audit.title: Audit journal
audit.description: Read-only history of role changes and cross-workspace configuration acts. Written by the server; hashes only, never values.

policy.title: Deployment policy
policy.description: The topmost configuration layer: values and locked prohibitions applied before every workspace and user layer. Credentials never belong here.
policy.llm_confirm_description: The change reaches every workspace and machine of this deployment on their next sync.
policy.kill_description: The deployment-wide kill switch: every MCP server is disabled and locked, and no workspace, user, or machine can turn MCP back on.
policy.kill_dialog_title: Disable MCP for the whole deployment?
policy.kill_dialog_description: Every MCP server of every workspace will be disabled and locked until this policy is lifted.
policy.unkill_description: The deployment-wide kill switch is lifted; workspace and user layers apply again.

workspaces.change_api_key: LLM API key is replaced with the new value
workspaces.change_base_url_cleared: LLM base URL: the stored value will be CLEARED
workspaces.change_model_cleared: LLM model: the stored value will be CLEARED
workspaces.config_confirm_description: The new values reach every member and machine of {{name}} on their next sync.
workspaces.config_description: The workspace layer between the deployment policy and the members' machines. The API key is write-only and never shown back.
workspaces.config_error: Couldn't read this workspace's configuration. Nothing below reflects what is actually stored.
workspaces.deactivate_confirm_description: Their sessions end, personal access tokens are revoked and live connections are closed. Tasks, comments and authorship stay intact, and the account can be restored.
workspaces.description: Every workspace of the deployment. Find one, then edit its configuration layer or place a personal override on one of its members — deployment role only, no membership needed.
workspaces.list_error: Couldn't load the deployment's workspaces. This is a failed read, not an empty deployment.
workspaces.no_identity: The server sent this row without an identifier — actions are unavailable.
workspaces.override_confirm_description: From the next sync this member's machines work through the substituted values instead of the workspace ones.
workspaces.override_dialog_description: Only the fields you fill in are overridden; everything else keeps following the workspace layer. The API key is write-only.
workspaces.override_not_read_yet: The personal override has not been read yet. Until it is, this form cannot show what is already set — only the fields you touch will be sent.
workspaces.override_read_error: Couldn't read this member's override. The fields below show nothing, which is not the same as "there is none".
workspaces.override_remove_confirm_description: The member falls back to the workspace layer and the deployment policy.
workspaces.overrides_error: Couldn't read the personal overrides of this workspace. Until this read succeeds, whether a member is overridden is unknown — and an override still takes precedence on that member's machines.
workspaces.reactivate_confirm_description: The block is lifted. Sessions and tokens issued before the deactivation stay dead — the person signs in again.
workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.toast_revoke_failed: The sessions could not be ended.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.description: Every machine of the deployment: who is alive, when it last checked in, which CLI it runs and where work is wedged. Read-only — the metrics stay the alerting surface, this is the roll-call.
fleet.empty: No machines have registered in this deployment yet.

mcp.title: Deployment MCP library
mcp.description: Shared MCP servers you author once for the whole deployment. Adding one here gives it to nobody: each workspace's owner or admin has to enable it, and only then can it be assigned to an agent.
mcp.write_only_note: Configurations are write-only: urls, commands, headers, and environment values are never sent back — to anyone, including you. Editing a record means entering its configuration again. What you store here is still handed to the runtime of every workspace that enables the record, so those workspace administrators can read it — keep only credentials the whole deployment may hold.
mcp.empty_description: Add a record here, then let each workspace decide whether to enable it.
mcp.delete_description: "{{name}}" will be removed from the deployment, from every workspace that enabled it, and from every agent it was assigned to.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.description: Shared MCP servers for this workspace. Adding one here gives it to no agent — assign it on an agent's MCP tab, where it also gets its own on/off switch.
mcp.write_only_note: Configurations are write-only: urls, commands, headers, and environment values are never sent back, so editing a server means entering its configuration again.
mcp.name_collision_note: A name that matches an MCP server the machine already defines — including one switched on through the workspace configuration defaults — REPLACES that entry wholesale, environment values included. Pick a distinct name unless replacing it is what you want.
mcp.empty_description: Add a server here, then assign it to the agents that should use it.
mcp.admin_only_note: Only workspace owners and admins can change this library.
mcp.save_failed_toast: Could not save the MCP server
mcp.remove_failed_toast: Could not remove the MCP server
mcp.delete_description: "{{name}}" will be removed from the workspace and from every agent it was assigned to.
mcp.deployment_note: Records marked "Deployment" come from the deployment library. A deployment administrator manages them; this workspace can take one or drop it, but not edit it.
mcp.offers_empty: The deployment offers no shared MCP servers.
mcp.offer_failed_toast: Could not change the deployment MCP server
mcp.credentials_description: These values are yours. Nobody else can read them — not a workspace admin, not the person who added this server. They are used only by the agents you own.
mcp.credentials_replace_placeholder: Already supplied — type a new value to replace it
mcp.credentials_still_missing: Still needed after this save: {{fields}}. Until every required field is supplied this server is left out of your agents' tasks.
mcp.credentials_missing_note: You have not supplied {{fields}}, so this server is left out of your agents' tasks.
mcp.credentials_supplied_note: You have supplied {{count}} of your credentials. That does not prove the server answers — it only means nothing is outstanding here.
mcp.schema_description: Declare which environment variables this server needs and where each one comes from. You are describing the form, not filling it in: every user supplies their own values, and you will never see them.
mcp.schema_label_label: Field name shown to the user
mcp.schema_hint_help: This text is the whole of what a blocked user is given to act on. Name the page, not just the product.
mcp.schema_required_label: Required — without it the server is left out of the user's tasks

security.recovery_warning: Save these now — they are shown once, each works once, and they are the only way in if you lose your phone.
security.required_notice: Your deployment requires a second factor on this account. Set one up now.
security.scan_hint: Scan this code with your authenticator app.

security.sessions_empty: No other devices are signed in.

deployment_sessions.absolute_hint: A session ends this long after it began, however actively it is used. 1–365.
deployment_sessions.defaults_note: Defaults with no policy set: {{idle}} hours idle, {{days}} days absolute, no session limit, no second factor required.
deployment_sessions.description: How long a session may live, how many one person may hold, and who must carry a second factor. Applies to the whole deployment.
deployment_sessions.idle_hint: A session with no requests for this long ends. 1–720.
deployment_sessions.max_hint: 0 means no limit. Above that, signing in on a new device ends the oldest session.
deployment_sessions.require_mfa_hint: Administrators is the recommended setting. Turning it on does not lock anyone out: people who have not enrolled are asked to, and can still sign in.
